description: Compact project-authored Python coding suite inspired by HumanEval+/MBPP+ task structure. Prompts are shown to the model; structured tests remain hidden from the model and are executed locally in a sandbox.
system_prompt: You are taking a deterministic Python coding benchmark. Return only valid Python 3 code. Define the requested function exactly. Do not use files, network access, subprocesses, input, eval, exec, or external packages.

tasks.prompt: Implement `clamp(value, low, high)`. Assume low <= high. Return low if value is below low, high if value is above high, otherwise return value.
Implement `dedupe_preserve_order(items)`. Return a new list containing only the first occurrence of each item, preserving the original order. Inputs contain hashable values.
Implement `is_palindrome_text(text)`. Return True when the letters and digits in text form a palindrome after ignoring case and all non-alphanumeric characters; otherwise return False.

args: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama!

tasks.prompt: Implement `second_largest_distinct(nums)`. Return the second-largest distinct value. Return None when fewer than two distinct values exist.
Implement `rotate_right(items, k)`. Return a new list rotated right by non-negative integer k positions. k may exceed the list length. An empty input returns an empty list.

Implement `balanced_brackets(text)`. Consider (), [], and {} brackets; ignore all other characters. Return True only if every opening bracket is closed by the matching type in the correct nesting order.
Implement `merge_intervals(intervals)`. Each interval is [start, end] with start <= end. Return intervals sorted by start with overlapping or touching intervals merged. Do not mutate the input.
Implement `longest_increasing_run(nums)`. Return the length of the longest contiguous strictly increasing run. Return 0 for an empty list.

Implement `word_frequencies(text)`. A word is a maximal consecutive sequence of ASCII letters A-Z or a-z. Return a dictionary mapping lowercase words to occurrence counts. Ignore all non-letter characters.
Implement `two_sum_indices(nums, target)`. Return the lexicographically smallest pair [i, j] with i < j and nums[i] + nums[j] == target. Return [] if no pair exists.
Implement `run_length_encode(text)`. Return consecutive character runs as a list of [character, count] pairs. Preserve characters exactly. An empty string returns [].
Implement `flatten_nested_list(value)`. value is a list whose elements may themselves be nested lists to any depth. Return a new flat list containing all non-list elements from left to right.
